title: Scam warning on a message
summary: A calm caution card under a message from another person when the text looks like a common scam pattern. It says what the message has and what to check, in one action. It never says the message is a scam.

kind.description: The one pattern to explain, picked by the scam detector in the registry priority order.

warning.description: The card under the message. The message itself shows as usual.

notes: Move, do not rewrite: BipeKit ScamDetector.swift and ScamWarning.swift (ScamDetector.warningKind(for:eventID:)), libraries/bipe ScamDetector.kt. The rules come from bipe-shared registries (scamWarningKindPriority, link and Pix patterns) and must match test-vectors/scam-warnings.json.

Input: MessageContent.body of a text message (MsgLikeKind.Message) from another person. Own messages, deleted messages and undecryptable messages get no card. Image captions are checked when media lands (#561).
The detector runs on the device. Nothing about the message or the warning leaves the phone. No analytics (plan section 2).
An edit keeps the event ID: the check runs again on the new body (the BipeKit cache keys on the body too).
Look: trust caution level from the design tokens (trust-ui.md): subtle caution background, caution border, a warning icon, title then the kind text. No red, no exclamation mark, no close button.
Screen readers read the card as one element: title, then the kind text.
